findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and can panic on nil toggles
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as the negation of IsEnabledGlobally, then returns false on both branches, so the feature flag is dead code and the intent is unreadable for anyone re-enabling SQL expressions later. It also dereferences h.features without a nil check: an ExpressionQueryReader constructed with nil FeatureToggles (as test and legacy callers do) will panic on a SQL query instead of returning the 'not implemented' error, turning a disabled-feature request into a server panic path.

findings.title: No tests cover the disabled SQL-expression behaviour and existing SQL tests are left broken
findings.body: The stub DB makes TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto always return 'not implemented', and reader.go now rejects QueryTypeSQL, but the PR adds or updates no tests. Existing tests that construct SQL commands via NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand will now fail with sql-invalid-sql instead of exercising SQL, and nothing verifies the security-critical contract that a SQL expression is rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. The disabled paths in reader.go, sql_command.go and pkg/expr/sql should be covered (and obsolete SQL-execution tests removed or skipped) before merging a CVE fix.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is not gated by the new disabled check
findings.body: Only ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery checks enableSqlExpressions; UnmarshalSQLCommand (the legacy rawNode pipeline entry point) still calls NewSQLCommand unconditionally. It is only stopped indirectly because sql.TablesList now errors from the stub DB, so legacy callers get a misleading BadRequest 'error reading SQL command' rather than an explicit disabled/not-implemented error, and restoring a real DB implementation in pkg/expr/sql would silently re-enable SQL expressions through this path despite the CVE fix. Gate UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand with the same disabled check.
